# SurfaceOne for Vue — setup

Vue 3 and Nuxt components of the SurfaceOne design system — the twins of
`@surface-one/angular`: the same tokens, skins and component stylesheets, the same markup
(`class`, `data-slot`, `data-variant`, …) and the same behaviour (focus, keyboard, ARIA).
Every component is `Sone*`, SSR-safe and tree-shakable.

```bash
npm install @surface-one/vue @surface-one/tokens
```

## Nuxt

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ["@surface-one/vue/nuxt"],
  surfaceOne: {
    // all optional
    messages: { close: "Zamknij", loading: "Ładowanie" },
    logoAssetBase: "/brand/",
  },
  app: {
    head: { htmlAttrs: { "data-skin": "studio", "data-theme": "system" } },
  },
});
```

The module adds the CSS (`@surface-one/tokens`, then `@surface-one/vue/styles.css`),
auto-imports every `Sone*` component (a page bundles only what it uses) and registers the
`v-sone-tooltip` directive. Options: `css`, `components` (both default `true`),
`messages`, `logoAssetBase`.

## Vue (Vite)

```ts
import { createApp } from "vue";
import { SurfaceOne } from "@surface-one/vue";
import "@surface-one/tokens";
import "@surface-one/vue/styles.css";

createApp(App)
  .use(SurfaceOne, { messages: { close: "Zamknij" } })
  .mount("#app");
```

`SurfaceOne` registers every component globally; pass `{ components: false }` and import
them where you use them (`import { SoneButton } from "@surface-one/vue"`).

## Only the CSS you use

`styles.css` holds every component (about 265 KB, 36 KB gzipped). To ship less, import
`dist/styles/<slug>.css` for each component you render (the slug is its kebab-case name:
`SoneButton` → `button`, `SoneDatePicker` → `date-picker`) and then `base.css` (native form
controls, the layout and text utilities, keyframes) in its place:

```ts
import "@surface-one/tokens";
import "@surface-one/vue/styles/button.css";
import "@surface-one/vue/styles/date-picker.css";
import "@surface-one/vue/styles/base.css";
```

Each file already carries the components it renders inside (`date-picker.css` brings the calendar,
the popover and the button), so one import per component you use is enough; with Nuxt, set `surfaceOne: { css: false }` and list `@surface-one/tokens` and these files in `css`. The build checks
that every component has its file and that together they hold every rule of `styles.css`.

## Theming

`@surface-one/tokens` is driven by three attributes on `<html>`: `data-skin`
(`surface` | `linen` | `studio` | `paper` | `minimalist` | `neumorphism`), `data-theme` (`light` | `dark` | `system`) and
`data-accent` (`blue` | `teal` | `green` | `orange` | `pink`).

## From Angular to Vue

| Angular                                           | Vue                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<button soneBtn variant="outline">`              | `<SoneButton variant="outline">`                                           |
| `<a soneBtn href="/x">`                           | `<SoneButton as="a" href="/x">` / `:as="NuxtLink" to=…`                    |
| `<div soneCard>` + `soneCardHeader` …             | `<SoneCard>` + `<SoneCardHeader>` …                                        |
| `<sone-switch [(checked)]="on">`                  | `<SoneSwitch v-model="on">`                                                |
| `<sone-select [(value)]>` / `sone-slider`         | `<SoneSelect v-model>` / `<SoneSlider v-model>`                            |
| `<sone-segmented [(value)]>`                      | `<SoneSegmented v-model :options>`                                         |
| `[soneToggleGroup] type="single" [(value)]`       | `<SoneToggleGroup type="single" v-model>` + items with `value`             |
| `[(expanded)]` / `[(open)]`                       | `v-model:expanded` / `v-model:open`                                        |
| `<sone-dialog [(open)]>` / `@if` + `(dismiss)`    | `<SoneDialog v-model:open>` or `v-if` + `@dismiss`                         |
| `<sone-table-column key>` / `[columns]`           | `:columns="[{ key, header }]"` + `#cell-<key>="{ row }"`                   |
| `<sone-search-field [(value)] (submit)>`          | `<SoneSearchField v-model @submit>`                                        |
| `soneConfirm` + `soneConfirmTitle` …              | `<SoneConfirm>` + `<SoneConfirmTitle>` …                                   |
| `[soneSectionHeadingActions]` projection          | the `#actions` slot                                                        |
| `[soneTooltip]="'Copy'"`                          | `v-sone-tooltip="'Copy'"` (`v-sone-tooltip:top` = side)                    |
| `$localize` strings                               | `messages` (plugin / module option, `provideSoneMessages`)                 |
| `provideSoneLogoAssets("/brand/")`                | `logoAssetBase` option (default `/brand/`)                                 |
| `<div soneSidebarWrapper>` + `SONE_SIDEBAR_PARTS` | `<SoneSidebarWrapper>` + `<SoneSidebar>`, `<SoneSidebarMenuButton>` …      |
| `SoneSidebarService` / `provideSoneSidebarConfig` | `useSoneSidebar()` / `provideSoneSidebar(config)`, the wrapper's `:config` |

A Nuxt link button: `import { NuxtLink } from "#components"` in `<script setup>`, then
`<SoneButton :as="NuxtLink" to="/pricing">` (`resolveComponent("NuxtLink")` does not work
here — Nuxt components are not registered globally).

Attribute directives become components that render the same element (change it with
`as`); every attribute and listener falls through to that element. Element components
render the same host tag (`<sone-icon>`, `<sone-switch>`, …), so the shared stylesheets
apply unchanged.

## Markdown

`<SoneMarkdown :source="text" />` renders untrusted markdown read-only, with the look of the
Angular `sone-markdown`: raw HTML is shown as text, links open in a new tab, images render only
from inline `data:` URLs, and everything goes through DOMPurify. The server renders the empty
host (there is no sanitizer without a DOM) and the browser fills it in once mounted. Install
`marked` and `dompurify` alongside it: they are optional peer dependencies.

`<SoneMarkdownEditor v-model="text" />` is the twin of `sone-markdown-editor`: a formatting
toolbar (`toolbar="full" | "minimal" | "document" | "none"`, ⌘/Ctrl + B, I, K, Shift+X, Shift+9),
Write / Preview tabs (`v-model:mode`) or a split view, list continuation on Enter and
paste-as-markdown; its template ref has `applyCommand`, `insertText`, `wrapSelection` and the
rest, and the `#tools`, `#footer` and `#preview` slots extend it. `live` swaps the textarea for a
live-preview editor built on CodeMirror: install `@codemirror/{commands,lang-markdown,language,
state,view}` and `@lezer/{common,highlight,markdown}` for it (optional peer dependencies too). It
loads on demand after mount, so the server renders only its empty host.

## Sidebar

`SoneSidebarWrapper` holds the sidebar state for its subtree (open or collapsed, the
dragged width) and toggles it on ⌘B / Ctrl+B. Pass `:config` (the same fields as the
Angular `SoneSidebarConfig`) or call `provideSoneSidebar(config)` in a component above it
to own the state; `useSoneSidebar()` reads it anywhere below. The open state and width
persist to `localStorage` under the same keys as `@surface-one/angular` (set
`openStorageKey` / `widthStorageKey` to `null` to opt out). They are read on mount, never
on the server, so a Nuxt page hydrates without a mismatch and then shows the stored state.

```vue
<SoneSidebarWrapper>
  <SoneSidebar collapsible="icon" role="navigation" aria-label="Workspace">
    <SoneSidebarContent>
      <SoneSidebarMenu>
        <SoneSidebarMenuItem>
          <SoneSidebarMenuButton :as="NuxtLink" to="/" is-active tooltip="Meetings">
            <SoneIcon icon="meetings" /><span>Meetings</span>
          </SoneSidebarMenuButton>
        </SoneSidebarMenuItem>
      </SoneSidebarMenu>
    </SoneSidebarContent>
    <SoneSidebarRail />
  </SoneSidebar>
  <SoneSidebarInset>…</SoneSidebarInset>
</SoneSidebarWrapper>
```

## Brand marks

`SoneLogo` loads its SVGs from `logoAssetBase` (default `/brand/`): copy
`node_modules/@surface-one/tokens/brand` into `public/brand/`.
